summary.text: A bond angle is the angle formed between three atoms across at least two bonds, and it is one of the parameters that describe a molecule's geometry.
The angles between the bonds that an atom forms depend only weakly on the rest of the molecule, so they are approximately local and transferable.
Bond angles are part of the geometry that influences a substance's reactivity, polarity, phase of matter, color and magnetism.

facts.label: Definition
facts.value: The angle formed between three atoms across at least two bonds

facts.label: Part of geometry
facts.value: One of the parameters fixing each atom's position

facts.label: How it is found
facts.value: Spectroscopic and diffraction methods, or computation

facts.label: Local property
facts.value: Depends only weakly on the rest of the molecule

items.prompt: A chemist knows the angle between two bonds at an atom in one molecule and expects a similar angle in a different molecule. Is that reasonable?

options.label: No, since every molecule rewrites all of its angles
Yes, but only if both molecules have the same number of atoms
No, since each angle depends on the whole molecule
Yes, since such angles depend only weakly on the rest of the molecule

items.explain: The angles between the bonds an atom forms depend only weakly on the rest of the molecule, so they are approximately local and transferable.

items.prompt: Three atoms are joined in a row by two bonds, and a chemist measures the opening between the two links at the middle atom. What is this measurement called?

options.label: A bond length
A torsional angle
A bond angle
A sigma bond

items.explain: The angle formed between three connected atoms across at least two bonds is a bond angle.

items.prompt: A student wants the sharpest possible picture of a molecule's geometry, bond angles included. What sample conditions suit best?

options.label: Cold, since warmth averages the structure over more shapes
Hot, since faster atoms settle into one fixed shape
Temperature never matters for measuring a geometry
Warm, since moderate heat sharpens every spectrum

items.explain: Molecular geometries are best determined at low temperature, because at higher temperatures the structure is averaged over more accessible geometries.

items.prompt: A chemist describes one angle using three atoms and another using four atoms bonded in a chain. Which pairing is right?

options.label: Three atoms: bond angle; four atoms: torsional angle
Three atoms: torsional angle; four atoms: bond angle
Both use three atoms, but in a different order
Both use four atoms, but at different places

items.explain: A bond angle is formed between three atoms; a torsional angle is the angle between the plane of the first three atoms and the plane of the last three of four.

items.prompt: Around one central atom with four other atoms attached, why can the bond angles not all be chosen independently?

options.label: Bond lengths force every angle to be identical
The four atoms must always lie in one flat plane
A mathematical relationship among them removes one free choice
Torsional angles override the bond angles

items.explain: A mathematical relationship among the bond angles for one central atom and four peripheral atoms removes one degree of freedom.

items.prompt: A chemist cannot measure a new molecule in the lab. How else could its geometry, including bond angles, be obtained?

options.label: Only by guessing from its chemical formula
By computing it with ab initio quantum chemistry methods
By counting the atoms and averaging their sizes
It cannot be obtained without a lab measurement

items.explain: Geometries can also be computed by ab initio quantum chemistry methods to high accuracy.
